questions.question: Who appointed the ‘Hunter Commission’ for Educational Reforms in 1882?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Ripon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hunter Commission was appointed in **1882** by **Lord Ripon**, the then Viceroy of India.
 
• The commission was tasked with evaluating the state of education in India and recommending reforms to improve access to education.
 
• It placed strong emphasis on the expansion of primary education, especially among rural communities and underprivileged sections.
 
• It advocated for the involvement of local self-governments to fund and manage primary education institutions.
 
• The commission also recommended the establishment of secondary schools to cater to the growing demand for higher education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Ripon:**

 
 
• Lord Ripon served as the Viceroy of India from **1880 to 1884**.
 
• He is known as the **Father of Local Self-Government in India** for his efforts in decentralizing administrative powers.
 
• Ripon implemented several reforms in education, local governance, and civil liberties.
 
 
 
• **Primary Education in Colonial India:**
 
 
• During the 19th century, education in India was limited to elite groups, while rural and underprivileged communities had minimal access.
 
• The Hunter Commission sought to address these disparities by promoting universal access to primary education.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Hunter Commission:**
 
 
• It marked a pivotal step in formalizing education policies in British India.
 
• The recommendations laid the groundwork for further education reforms in the 20th century.
 
 
 
• **Local Self-Government:**
 
 
• Ripon encouraged local self-governments to take responsibility for funding and managing schools.
 
• This approach empowered local bodies and improved accountability in education delivery.

questions.question: The concept of the Self-Help Group Bank Linkage Program was introduced by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NABARD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Self-Help Group Bank Linkage Program (SHG-BLP)** was initiated by **NABARD** in 1992, marking a significant milestone in microfinance.
 
• The program aims to link **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**, typically formed by poor women, with banks to provide them access to formal financial services.
 
• It is considered the **world’s largest microfinance initiative**, with millions of SHGs formed and linked to banks across India.
 
• The program focuses on **empowering the rural poor** by providing them with financial resources to engage in income-generating activities.
 
• By 2023, it has helped **enhance financial inclusion** and enabled women in rural areas to improve their livelihoods and economic independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **What is NABARD?**

 
 
• **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)** is an apex development financial institution in India, established in **1982**.
 
• It focuses on **agriculture, rural development, and financial inclusion**.
 
• NABARD plays a key role in implementing and financing rural development schemes.
 
 
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs):**
 
 
• SHGs are **informal groups of 10-20 people**, usually women, who come together to save and borrow money collectively.
 
• They promote **self-reliance and economic empowerment**.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of SHG-BLP:**
 
 
• Encourages savings among SHG members and links them to **formal banking institutions**.
 
• Provides **collateral-free loans** to members to support income-generating activities.
 
• Promotes group accountability and peer monitoring to ensure repayment.
 
 
 
• **Impact of SHG-BLP:**
 
 
• Enhanced **financial literacy** and inclusion in rural areas.
 
• Empowered women by increasing their participation in economic activities.
 
• Boosted rural entrepreneurship and poverty alleviation.

questions.question: In which year did India host the FIFA U 17 Women's Football World Cup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2022**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup was hosted by **India in 2022**, marking a significant milestone for women's football in the country.
 
• The tournament took place between **October 11 and October 30, 2022**, with matches held in Bhubaneswar, Goa, and Navi Mumbai.
 
• This was the **second FIFA tournament hosted by India**, following the FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup held in 2017.
 
• The event aimed to **promote gender equality** and encourage the growth of women's football in India.
 
• Spain won the tournament, defeating Colombia 1-0 in the final held at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup:**

 
 
• It is a biennial football competition organized by FIFA for female players under the age of 17.
 
• The tournament was first held in **2008**, with New Zealand hosting the inaugural edition.
 
• It provides a platform for young talent to showcase their skills on the global stage.
 
 
 
• **India's Football Development:**
 
 
• Hosting the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup was part of India's efforts to **boost football infrastructure and popularity**.
 
• India also launched initiatives such as the **Football for All program** to promote grassroots participation.
 
 
 
• **DY Patil Stadium:**
 
 
• Located in Navi Mumbai, the DY Patil Stadium is one of India's premier sports venues.
 
• It hosted the **final match** of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022.
 
 
 
• **Spain's Victory:**
 
 
• Spain's win in 2022 was their **second consecutive FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title**, having won the tournament in 2018.
 
• The team's success highlighted their dominance in youth football globally.

questions.question: Which famous monument of Vijayapura has a Whispering Gallery, where subtle sounds can be heard clearly even from a distance of 37 metres?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gol Gumbaz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gol Gumbaz**, located in Vijayapura (Bijapur), Karnataka, is renowned for its **Whispering Gallery**, where even the faintest sound echoes and can be heard clearly up to 37 meters away.
 
• It is the **mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah**, the Sultan of Bijapur, and was built in 1656.
 
• The structure is known for its **massive dome**, which is one of the largest unsupported domes in the world.
 
• The Whispering Gallery runs along the periphery of the dome and is an architectural wonder due to its acoustic properties.
 
• Gol Gumbaz is an iconic example of **Deccan Sultanate architecture**, showcasing Indo-Islamic design influences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Architectural Features**:

 
 
• The Gol Gumbaz dome has a diameter of 44 meters, making it the second-largest pre-modern dome in the world.
 
• It is supported by eight intersecting arches and has no central pillar, which is a remarkable engineering feat.
 
 
 
• **Acoustics of the Whispering Gallery**:
 
 
• The gallery allows sound to travel across the dome, amplifying even the faintest whispers.
 
• This unique feature results from the dome's curvature and precise architectural design.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• Mohammed Adil Shah commissioned the structure to serve as his final resting place.
 
• The monument reflects the grandeur and cultural advancements of the Deccan Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Tourist Attraction**:
 
 
• Gol Gumbaz is one of the most visited historical sites in Karnataka, attracting tourists and architecture enthusiasts worldwide.
 
• The site also houses a museum showcasing artifacts from the Adil Shahi dynasty.

questions.question: __________ was an Indian mandolinist who was a master composer of the Carnatic style of classical music.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uppalapu Srinivas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Uppalapu Srinivas, popularly known as U. Srinivas, was a renowned **Indian mandolinist** and composer.
 
• He is credited with adapting the western mandolin to suit the **Carnatic style of classical music**.
 
• Srinivas performed his first major concert at the age of **9** during the Thyagaraja Aradhana festival at Kumbakonam.
 
• He was a recipient of prestigious awards like the **Padma Shri** in 1998 and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in 2009.
 
• Uppalapu Srinivas is often referred to as the **"Mandolin Maestro"** for his exceptional contribution to Indian classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mandolin:**

 
 
• The mandolin is a stringed musical instrument in the lute family, typically played with a plectrum.
 
• It was originally a western instrument, but artists like U. Srinivas adapted it for Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• Carnatic music is a system of classical music associated with the southern part of India.
 
• It emphasizes vocal music and is characterized by intricate rhythmic patterns and improvisations.
 
 
 
• **Thyagaraja Aradhana:**
 
 
• An annual festival held in honor of Saint Thyagaraja, one of the greatest composers of Carnatic music.
 
• The event takes place in Thiruvaiyaru, Tamil Nadu, and attracts musicians and enthusiasts from around the world.
 
 
 
• **Notable Works of U. Srinivas:**
 
 
• Srinivas collaborated with global artists such as John McLaughlin and Michael Nyman, showcasing his versatility.
 
• He was part of the fusion group **Remember Shakti**, blending Indian classical with jazz.

questions.question: In which of the following dance performance is the main percussion instrument Edakka used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Edakka** is a prominent percussion instrument used in the classical dance form **Mohiniattam**, which originates from Kerala, India.
 
• The instrument produces soft and melodious sounds and is considered an essential part of the **musical accompaniment** for Mohiniattam performances.
 
• Mohiniattam is characterized by graceful movements, subtle expressions, and a repertoire that integrates **classical Carnatic music**.
 
• The **Edakka** is played with the hands, and its sound complements the lyrical and emotive nature of Mohiniattam.
 
• Other instruments like Veena, Mridangam, and Flute also accompany Mohiniattam performances, but the Edakka holds a unique place in its musical ensemble.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohiniattam:**

 
 
• It is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• Mohiniattam translates to "Dance of the Enchantress" and is deeply rooted in the **Lasya** (feminine and graceful) aspect of classical dance.
 
• The dance form traditionally narrates stories from Hindu mythology, especially focusing on Lord Vishnu and his incarnations.
 
 
 
• **Edakka:**
 
 
• Also known as "Idakka," it is a traditional drum of Kerala used in temple rituals and classical music.
 
• Its construction involves a wooden drum with leather membranes, and it is known for its versatility in producing tonal variations.
 
• The Edakka is often associated with temple art forms like Kathakali and Mohiniattam.
 
 
 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India:**
 
 
• India has eight officially recognized classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Sattriya, and Mohiniattam.
 
• Each dance form has unique features, costumes, musical instruments, and regional significance.
 
 
 
• **Role of Music in Classical Dance:**
 
 
• Music plays a vital role in classical dance, helping to set the mood, rhythm, and narrative flow.
 
• Instruments like Mridangam, Veena, Flute, and Edakka are commonly used to complement the dancer's movements and expressions.

questions.question: The Government of India in collaboration with ________ has launched the Skills on Wheels mission in Oct 2023 for equipping rural youth with employable skills.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IndusInd Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India launched the **Skills on Wheels Mission** in October 2023, aiming to empower rural youth with employable skills.
 
• The initiative is being implemented in collaboration with **IndusInd Bank**, which plays a key role in supporting the mission.
 
• The Skills on Wheels Mission focuses on providing mobile training units that reach remote and rural areas to offer skill development programs.
 
• These programs target sectors such as **healthcare, IT, retail, and manufacturing** to increase employability among rural youth.
 
• The mission aligns with the Government’s broader goals under the **Skill India initiative** to create a skilled workforce by 2030.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Skill India Mission:**

 
 
• Launched in 2015, the Skill India Mission aims to train over 40 crore people in India across various sectors by 2022.
 
• It includes programs like **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)** for short-term training and recognition of prior learning.
 
 
 
• **Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) in Skill Development:**
 
 
• PPPs are collaborations between the government and private organizations like **IndusInd Bank** to improve outreach and efficiency.
 
• They provide funding, expertise, and infrastructure to ensure the success of skill development programs.
 
 
 
• **Mobile Training Units:**
 
 
• These units are equipped with tools, trainers, and resources to deliver skill training in remote and underserved areas.
 
• They help overcome geographical barriers and ensure inclusivity in skill development initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Rural Employment Challenges:**
 
 
• Youth in rural areas often face challenges like lack of access to quality education, training facilities, and employment opportunities.
 
• Government initiatives like Skills on Wheels aim to bridge these gaps and create sustainable livelihoods.

questions.question: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award is given for the spectacular and most outstanding performance in the field of sports by a sportsperson over a period of the previous four years. In 2021, the awardee for para shooting was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Avani Lekhara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Avani Lekhara** was awarded the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2021 for her outstanding performance in para shooting.
 
• She became the first Indian woman to win a **gold medal** in shooting at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games.
 
• Avani won the gold medal in the **Women's 10m Air Rifle Standing (SH1)** event at the Paralympics with a record-breaking score.
 
• She also secured a **bronze medal** in the Women's 50m Rifle 3 Positions (SH1) event, making her the first Indian woman to win multiple medals at the Paralympics.
 
• Her achievements reflect resilience, determination, and contribution to para sports in India, earning her the prestigious award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**

 
 
• The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award is India’s highest sporting honor, established in 1991-1992.
 
• It is given to athletes for their spectacular and outstanding performance over the previous four years.
 
• The award consists of a medallion, certificate, and a cash prize of Rs. 25 lakh.
 
 
 
• **Para Shooting Classification:**
 
 
• The SH1 classification is for athletes who have an impairment that affects their legs but allows them to support the rifle without any aids.
 
• Events are conducted in different positions, such as standing, kneeling, and prone.
 
 
 
• **Tokyo 2020 Paralympics:**
 
 
• The Tokyo Paralympics were held from August 24 to September 5, 2021.
 
• India achieved its best-ever medal tally in a single Paralympic Games with 19 medals, including 5 golds.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian Paralympic Achievers in 2021:**
 
 
• Neeraj Chopra won India’s first-ever Olympic gold in athletics but was not a Paralympian.
 
• Chanu Saikhom Mirabai secured a silver medal at the Tokyo Olympics in weightlifting.
 
• Other notable Paralympic medalists include Sumit Antil (gold in javelin throw) and Krishna Nagar (gold in badminton).

questions.question: What is the tenure of a Governor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tenure of a Governor in India is **5 years**, as per Article 156 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor holds office **at the pleasure of the President** and may resign before completing their tenure.
 
• The 5-year term is counted from the date they take the **oath of office**.
 
• Governors can be reappointed or transferred to other states, and they may **continue in office even after their term ends** until a successor is appointed.
 
• Although the term is 5 years, the President has the authority to **remove a Governor** before the completion of their term without any justification.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 153:** There shall be a Governor for each state in India; however, one person can act as the Governor for two or more states.
 
• **Appointment:** The Governor is appointed by the President of India and is considered the constitutional head of the state.
 
• **Oath of Office:** The Governor takes an oath before the Chief Justice of the High Court of the concerned state or the senior-most judge available.
 
• **Eligibility:** To be appointed as a Governor, a person must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years of age, and should not hold any office of profit.
 
• **Role:** The Governor acts as the link between the state government and the central government and plays a crucial role in the administration of the state under the provisions of the Constitution.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about the Cholas?

1 The capital of the Chola kingdom was Tanjore.

2 Vikram Chola had in his veins the blood of the Cholas and Eastern Chalukyas.

3 Rajendra I Chola is known as Gangaikonda Chola.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All 1, 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The capital of the Chola kingdom was Tanjore (Thanjavur):** Thanjavur served as the political, cultural, and religious center of the Chola Empire.
 
• **Vikram Chola's lineage:** Vikram Chola, a notable ruler of the Chola dynasty, was a descendant of both the Cholas and the Eastern Chalukyas, showcasing the dynastic alliances of the period.
 
• **Gangaikonda Chola:** Rajendra I Chola earned the title "Gangaikonda Chola" after his victorious expedition to the Ganges River, symbolizing his expansionist policies.
 
• The Cholas were known for their contributions to art, architecture, and administration, with temples like the Brihadeeswarar Temple standing as a testament to their legacy.
 
• The Chola dynasty played a significant role in maritime trade and had extensive influence in Southeast Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chola Administration:** The Cholas implemented an efficient administrative system, including well-organized village assemblies (sabhas) that managed local affairs.
 
• **Temple Architecture:** The Cholas are renowned for their monumental temple architecture, especially the Brihadeeswarar Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• **Naval Power:** The Chola Empire had a powerful navy, enabling them to establish trade and cultural ties with Southeast Asia, including the Srivijaya Empire.
 
• **Literary Contributions:** The Chola period saw significant advancements in Tamil literature, with works like Kamba Ramayanam being composed during their reign.
 
• **Gangaikonda Cholapuram:** Rajendra I established Gangaikonda Cholapuram as a new capital to commemorate his conquests and to signify the Chola Empire's dominance.

questions.question: How many artists are selected for the one-time Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award, 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award 2022** was introduced as part of the celebration of India’s 75th year of independence under the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav initiative.
 
• A total of **86 artists**, aged above 75 years and who have not been recipients of any National Honour in their careers, were selected for this one-time award.
 
• The award aims to honor senior artists for their lifetime contribution to Indian performing arts, including music, dance, and theater.
 
• Recipients of the award were recognized for their dedication to preserving and propagating India's cultural heritage.
 
• The award was presented by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, the apex body for performing arts in India, functioning under the Ministry of Culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi:**

 
 
• Established in 1952, it is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama.
 
• It functions as an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture.
 
• The Akademi promotes, preserves, and documents India’s diverse performing arts heritage.
 
 
 
• **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav:**
 
 
• A government initiative launched in March 2021 to commemorate 75 years of India’s independence.
 
• It focuses on celebrating India's cultural, historical, and developmental milestones.
 
• Activities under this initiative include awards, exhibitions, workshops, and cultural programs.
 
 
 
• **Performing Arts in India:**
 
 
• India has a rich tradition of performing arts, including classical dance forms like Bharatanatyam, Kathak, and Odissi.
 
• Classical music forms include Hindustani and Carnatic traditions, with numerous regional variations.
 
• Theater and folk performances like Yakshagana and Nautanki represent India's regional diversity.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Culture:**
 
 
• Responsible for the preservation and promotion of India’s cultural heritage.
 
• Oversees institutions like the Sangeet Natak Akademi, Lalit Kala Akademi, and National School of Drama.
 
• Organizes initiatives like the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat program to foster cultural unity.

questions.question: Which of the following sessions of the Indian National Congress was headed by Sarojini Naidu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanpur, 1925**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kanpur Session of 1925** was presided over by **Sarojini Naidu**, making her the first Indian woman to head the Indian National Congress.
 
• Her election as the president marked a significant milestone in the history of the Indian freedom struggle, showcasing the role of women leaders.
 
• During her tenure as the Congress president, Sarojini Naidu emphasized the importance of communal harmony and national unity.
 
• The session contributed to promoting the Gandhian ideals of Swaraj and non-violence as central tenets of the freedom movement.
 
• Sarojini Naidu was also known as the "Nightingale of India" for her contributions to Indian poetry and her eloquence in addressing public gatherings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress:**

 
 
• Founded in **1885**, the Indian National Congress was pivotal in the Indian independence movement.
 
• It was initially established to create a platform for civil and political dialogue among educated Indians.
 
 
 
• **Role of Women in the Freedom Struggle:**
 
 
• Women leaders like Sarojini Naidu, Annie Besant, and Kamala Nehru played key roles in shaping India's independence movement.
 
• They contributed through speeches, protests, and active participation in leadership roles.
 
 
 
• **Gandhian Philosophy:**
 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi advocated for Swaraj (self-rule), non-violence, and communal harmony as the pillars of the freedom struggle.
 
• These ideals were deeply ingrained in Congress sessions and activities during the independence movement.
 
 
 
• **Sarojini Naidu's Legacy:**
 
 
• She served as the Governor of Uttar Pradesh post-independence, becoming the first woman to hold a governorship in independent India.
 
• Her poetry, speeches, and activism continue to inspire generations in India and globally.

questions.question: Which local storm is also known as 'Kalbaisakhi'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nor Westers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nor Westers** are locally known as **'Kalbaisakhi'** in West Bengal and parts of Eastern India.
 
• These storms occur predominantly during the **pre-monsoon season**, typically from March to May.
 
• Nor Westers are characterized by **sudden, violent thunderstorms** accompanied by heavy rain and strong winds.
 
• These storms are particularly beneficial for agriculture as they help in **irrigating crops like mango, jute, and rice**.
 
• They are most common in areas such as **West Bengal, Assam, Odisha, and Jharkhand**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Formation of Nor Westers:**

 
 
• Nor Westers are caused by the interaction of warm, moist air from the Bay of Bengal and cool, dry air from northern India.
 
• The instability in the atmosphere leads to the formation of cumulonimbus clouds, resulting in thunderstorms.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Mango Cultivation:**
 
 
• Nor Westers are referred to as 'Mango Showers' in other parts of India as they aid in the ripening of mangoes.
 
• The rains from these storms are crucial for improving fruit quality and yield.
 
 
 
• **Associated Weather Phenomena:**
 
 
• These storms can cause hail, which sometimes damages crops and property.
 
• High winds and lightning are common features of Nor Westers, occasionally leading to fatalities and infrastructural damage.
 
 
 
• **Regional Names:**
 
 
• In West Bengal and Assam, they are called 'Kalbaisakhi,' meaning 'Calamity of the Month of Vaisakh.'
 
• In Kerala and coastal Karnataka, similar pre-monsoon rains are referred to as 'Mango Showers.'

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Milad-un-Nabi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Milad-un-Nabi**, also known as Mawlid, is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad, the founder of Islam.
 
• It is observed on the **12th day of the Islamic month of Rabi-ul-Awwal**, as per the Hijri lunar calendar.
 
• The festival is marked by **prayers, sermons, and recitations** of the Quran, focusing on the life and teachings of Prophet Muhammad.
 
• Muslims across the world organize religious gatherings, processions, and charitable activities on this day.
 
• The event is particularly significant for Sunni Muslims, while many Shia Muslims celebrate the birth of the Prophet on a different date.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prophet Muhammad:**

 
 
• Born in **570 CE** in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, Prophet Muhammad is considered the last prophet in Islam.
 
• He received revelations from Allah through the angel Gabriel, which are compiled in the Islamic holy book, the Quran.
 
 
 
• **Rabi-ul-Awwal:**
 
 
• It is the third month in the Islamic lunar calendar and holds religious significance for Muslims.
 
• Several important events in the Prophet's life, including his migration from Mecca to Medina, occurred in this month.
 
 
 
• **Celebration Practices:**
 
 
• Milad-un-Nabi is celebrated differently across countries, with traditions varying from region to region.
 
• In some places, people decorate streets, mosques, and homes with lights and banners.
 
• Charitable acts, such as distributing food and clothing to the needy, are emphasized during the festival.
 
 
 
• **Controversies:**
 
 
• While many Muslims celebrate Milad-un-Nabi, some Islamic scholars and groups believe that such celebrations are not part of the original teachings of Islam.
 
• These debates revolve around the permissibility of innovations (bid'ah) in religious practices.

questions.question: Which substance is commonly added to tap water to make it safe for drinking by killing harmful microorganisms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chlorine is widely used to disinfect water as it is highly effective in killing bacteria, viruses, and other harmful microorganisms.
 
• Water chlorination is a common practice in municipal water treatment plants worldwide to ensure drinking water is safe.
 
• Chlorine works by breaking down the cell walls of microorganisms, thereby inactivating or destroying them.
 
• In addition to disinfection, chlorine also helps to control algae and remove unpleasant tastes and odors caused by organic compounds in water.
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) recognizes chlorination as a key method for improving drinking water safety globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Free Chlorine:**

 
 
• This refers to the chlorine available in water to disinfect, which includes hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and hypochlorite ions (OCl-).
 
• The recommended level of free chlorine in drinking water is 0.2–0.5 mg/L to ensure effective disinfection.
 
 
 
• **Chlorination Byproducts:**
 
 
• When chlorine reacts with natural organic matter in water, it can form byproducts such as trihalomethanes (THMs).
 
• While these byproducts are monitored, the risk they pose is much lower than the risk of consuming untreated water.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Disinfection Methods:**
 
 
• Other methods like ozone treatment and UV radiation are also used for water disinfection, but chlorination remains the most economical and widely used.
 
 
 
• **History of Chlorination:**
 
 
• Water chlorination was first introduced in the late 19th and early 20th centuries to combat waterborne diseases like cholera and typhoid.
 
• The first continuous chlorination of public water supplies was in Jersey City, New Jersey, in 1908.
 
 
 
• **Health Benefits:**
 
 
• Chlorinated water significantly reduces the prevalence of waterborne diseases such as diarrhea, dysentery, and hepatitis A.
 
• It plays a critical role in achieving public health goals related to safe drinking water.

questions.question: Which of the following sectors engaged the largest percentage of women workers in the year 2019-2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Agriculture engaged the **largest percentage of women workers** in India during the year 2019-2020.
 
• According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), a significant proportion of rural women workers were employed in **agricultural activities**, including crop production, livestock rearing, and allied tasks.
 
• Women constituted around **55%-60% of the agricultural labor force** in India, highlighting their critical role in the sector.
 
• Tasks performed by women in agriculture include **sowing, weeding, harvesting, and post-harvest processing**, which are essential for agricultural productivity.
 
• The dependency on agriculture for livelihoods remains high among rural women due to limited opportunities in other sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gender Roles in Agriculture:**

 
 
• Women in agriculture often perform labor-intensive tasks and are involved in both subsistence farming and commercial crop production.
 
• They contribute significantly to food security but face challenges such as limited access to resources, training, and decision-making power.
 
 
 
• **Rural Employment Trends:**
 
 
• Rural areas in India show a higher dependency on agriculture for employment, particularly among women.
 
• Non-farm opportunities like manufacturing and services are gradually increasing but remain limited for women.
 
 
 
• **Livelihood Diversification:**
 
 
• In recent years, women have started diversifying their livelihoods into allied sectors like **dairy farming, poultry, and fisheries** to supplement household incomes.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Women’s Agricultural Work:**
 
 
• Women face challenges like **low wages, lack of land ownership, and limited access to credit**.
 
• Policy interventions like the **National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA)** aim to provide equal opportunities and fair wages to women workers.

questions.question: Which region in India has the highest concentration of Iron and Steel Industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chotanagpur plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Chotanagpur Plateau**, located in eastern India, specifically in Jharkhand, is rich in mineral resources, including iron ore, coal, and bauxite, making it the hub for iron and steel industries.
 
• Prominent iron and steel plants such as **Tata Steel (Jamshedpur)**, **Bokaro Steel Plant**, and **Rourkela Steel Plant** are situated in and around this region.
 
• The availability of high-grade iron ore and coal in close proximity ensures lower transportation costs and efficient production processes for steel manufacturing.
 
• This plateau is also strategically located near major rivers such as Damodar and Subarnarekha, ensuring water supply for industrial operations.
 
• Chotanagpur’s mineral-rich geology and infrastructure contribute to it being the backbone of India's iron and steel industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Ore:**

 
 
• India is one of the leading producers of iron ore globally, with deposits found mainly in Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, and Goa.
 
• Iron ore is the primary raw material used in steel production, accounting for 98% of mined iron globally.
 
 
 
• **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC):**
 
 
• Established in 1948, DVC serves as a critical source of power and water supply for industries in the Chotanagpur Plateau.
 
• Its thermal power plants are key contributors to the industrial energy needs of the region.
 
 
 
• **Tata Steel:**
 
 
• Founded in 1907, Tata Steel's Jamshedpur plant is India’s oldest steel manufacturing facility and is located in the Chotanagpur Plateau.
 
• It played a pivotal role in the industrialization of India and continues to be a global leader in steel production.
 
 
 
• **Steel Industry in India:**
 
 
• India is the second-largest producer of steel globally, with a production capacity exceeding 120 million tonnes annually.
 
• The iron and steel industry is crucial to India's economy, contributing significantly to infrastructure development, manufacturing, and exports.

questions.question: During the framing of the Indian Constitution, the Constituent Assembly held a total of eleven sessions, with sittings spread over for how many days?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**165**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constituent Assembly of India was established in **1946** to draft the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Assembly held a total of **eleven sessions** between December 1946 and January 1950.
 
• The sittings of the Constituent Assembly were spread over **165 days**, during which deliberations on various aspects of the Constitution took place.
 
• The Constituent Assembly adopted the final draft of the Constitution on **26th November 1949**, which came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the **Drafting Committee**, which played a pivotal role in framing the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constituent Assembly Membership:**

 
 
• The Assembly initially had **389 members**, which was later reduced to 299 after the partition of India.
 
• Members were elected indirectly by the provincial assemblies under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.
 
 
 
• **Sessions of the Assembly:**
 
 
• The first session was held on **9th December 1946**, presided over by Dr. Sachidananda Sinha as the temporary chairman.
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was later elected as the permanent President of the Assembly.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution is the **longest written constitution** in the world.
 
• It incorporates features of various constitutions, including parliamentary democracy, federalism, and fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Drafting Committee:**
 
 
• The Drafting Committee, chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, was responsible for preparing the draft of the Constitution.
 
• The committee worked for **two years, eleven months, and eighteen days** to finalize the draft.

questions.question: The title of the autobiography of famous cricketer of Pakistan Imran Khan is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All Round View**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **All Round View** is the autobiography of **Imran Khan**, one of Pakistan's most renowned cricketers, published in **1992**.
 
• The book reflects on Imran Khan’s cricketing journey, life experiences, and his transition from a cricketer to a philanthropist and politician.
 
• The autobiography provides insights into his leadership as the captain of the Pakistan cricket team, including the iconic **1992 Cricket World Cup victory**.
 
• It also discusses Khan’s personal life, his philanthropic efforts such as establishing the **Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital**, and his vision for Pakistan’s development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Imran Khan’s Cricketing Achievements:**

 
 
• Imran Khan is regarded as one of the greatest all-rounders in cricket history.
 
• He captained Pakistan to its first and only **Cricket World Cup victory in 1992**.
 
• He played 88 Test matches and 175 One-Day Internationals during his career, achieving impressive bowling and batting records.
 
 
 
• **Philanthropic Contributions:**
 
 
• Imran Khan founded the **Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital** in Lahore in 1994, which provides free treatment to underprivileged cancer patients.
 
• He also established the **Namal University** in Mianwali, Pakistan, aiming to provide quality education in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Political Career:**
 
 
• Imran Khan founded the political party **Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)** in 1996.
 
• He served as the **Prime Minister of Pakistan** from August 2018 to April 2022.
 
• His political vision focuses on anti-corruption, poverty alleviation, and national development.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Imran Khan’s autobiography, **All Round View**, is considered a reflection of his dynamic personality and achievements.
 
• He continues to be an influential figure in cricket, philanthropy, and politics.

questions.question: Why will a person weigh more at the north or south pole?

options.text: Due to Earth’s distance from the sun
Due to variation in centrifugal force of earth with latitude
Due to variation in centripetal force of earth with altitude
Due to variation in centripetal force of earth with latitude

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Due to variation in centrifugal force of earth with latitude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The centrifugal force on Earth is caused by its rotation and is strongest at the equator due to the higher rotational velocity.
 
• At the poles, the centrifugal force is negligible as the poles do not experience the same rotational velocity as the equator.
 
• Less centrifugal force at the poles reduces the outward "push," causing a person to weigh more compared to their weight at the equator.
 
• Earth’s shape, which is slightly oblate (flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator), also contributes to the variation in weight.
 
• The gravitational force is slightly stronger at the poles due to the reduced distance from the Earth’s center compared to the equator.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centrifugal Force:** A pseudo-force that acts outward on a mass when it is rotating, proportional to the rotational velocity and the radius of rotation.
 
• **Earth’s Shape:** The Earth is an oblate spheroid; it is flatter at the poles and bulges at the equator, influencing gravity and centrifugal forces.
 
• ** Gravity is slightly stronger at the poles because they are closer to the Earth’s center compared to the equator.
 
• Weight vs Mass:** Weight is the force exerted due to gravity and varies with location, while mass remains constant regardless of location.
 
• **Rotational Impact:** Earth’s rotation affects the distribution of centrifugal force, which contributes to the difference in apparent weight across latitudes.

questions.question: For most of the ecosystem, what is the primary source of energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sunlight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sunlight** is the primary source of energy for most ecosystems as it drives the process of **photosynthesis**, enabling plants to produce food. 
 
• Through photosynthesis, plants convert sunlight into chemical energy, which becomes the foundation for the food chain in ecosystems.
 
• Sunlight provides energy directly to producers (plants, algae, cyanobacteria), which are then consumed by herbivores and higher-level consumers.
 
• Solar energy also influences critical environmental factors, such as temperature and climate, which directly impact ecosystems.
 
• Without sunlight, ecosystems would collapse as the flow of energy through trophic levels would cease to function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis:** A biochemical process in which green plants, algae, and some bacteria use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to produce glucose and oxygen. 
 
• **Energy Flow in Ecosystems:** The transfer of energy begins with producers (plants) and moves through consumers (herbivores, carnivores) and decomposers (fungi, bacteria). 
 
• **Autotrophs:** Organisms like plants and algae that produce their own food using sunlight are known as autotrophs or primary producers.
 
• **Trophic Levels:** Each level in a food chain represents a trophic level, starting with producers, followed by primary consumers, secondary consumers, and tertiary consumers. 
 
• **Solar Radiation:** Nearly 70% of solar energy reaching Earth is absorbed by the atmosphere, land, and oceans, while the rest is reflected back into space.

questions.question: Which poet composed the Allahabad Prashasti of Samudragupta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harisena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Allahabad Prashasti (also known as the Prayag Prashasti) was composed by **Harisena**, a court poet and minister of Samudragupta.
 
• Harisena served as the **Mahadandanayaka** (Chief Judicial Officer) and **Sandhivigrahika** (Minister of Peace and War) under Samudragupta.
 
• The Prashasti is inscribed on an **Ashokan pillar** located in Allahabad (Prayagraj).
 
• This inscription provides a detailed account of Samudragupta's conquests, achievements, and patronage of art and culture.
 
• It is written in **Sanskrit** and is considered a classic example of eulogy in Indian inscriptions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samudragupta**:

 
 
• Samudragupta (c. 335–380 CE) was one of the greatest rulers of the Gupta Empire.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Napoleon of India" due to his military conquests and expansion of the empire.
 
• He was a patron of art, music, and literature, and his reign marked the beginning of the classical age in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Prashasti:**
 
 
• A Prashasti is an inscription written in praise of a ruler or a patron, often highlighting their achievements and virtues.
 
• The term "Prashasti" means "praise" in Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Ashokan Pillars:**
 
 
• The Allahabad pillar is one of the many pillars erected by Emperor Ashoka during his reign in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• These pillars were later reused by subsequent rulers for inscriptions, such as Samudragupta's Allahabad Prashasti.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire:**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire (c. 319–550 CE) is often referred to as the "Golden Age" of India due to its advancements in science, art, and culture.
 
• It witnessed significant achievements in fields such as mathematics, astronomy, literature, and architecture.

questions.question: Which Indian state's cabinet approved the proposal for recommending the inclusion of the Kui language in the eighth schedule in July 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Odisha state cabinet approved the proposal to recommend the inclusion of the Kui language in the eighth schedule of the Constitution in July 2023.
 
• Kui is primarily spoken by the Kandha tribe, one of the largest tribal groups in Odisha.
 
• The move aims to provide recognition and promote the preservation of the Kui language and culture.
 
• The eighth schedule of the Indian Constitution lists official languages recognized by the Indian government.
 
• Odisha has been proactive in protecting and promoting tribal languages and heritage through such initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kui Language:**

 
 
• Kui is a Dravidian language spoken by the Kandha tribe, predominantly in Odisha.
 
• It is considered an endangered language with efforts being made to preserve its linguistic and cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• The eighth schedule currently lists 22 languages recognized as official languages in India.
 
• Inclusion in the eighth schedule provides constitutional protection and government support for the development of the language.
 
 
 
• **Kandha Tribe:**
 
 
• The Kandha tribe is one of the major Scheduled Tribes in Odisha, known for their rich cultural heritage and traditions.
 
• They primarily reside in districts such as Kandhamal, Rayagada, and Kalahandi.
 
 
 
• **Language Preservation Efforts:**
 
 
• India has been actively working towards safeguarding indigenous and tribal languages through policy measures and community participation.
 
• Preserving tribal languages is crucial for maintaining cultural diversity and heritage in the country.

questions.question: According to the census of India 2011, which union territory of India has the highest literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshadweep**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, **Lakshadweep** recorded the highest literacy rate among Union Territories, at **91.85%**.
 
• The literacy rate represents the percentage of the population aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• Lakshadweep's high literacy rate is attributed to effective educational policies and programs implemented in the region.
 
• Kerala, which is often associated with high literacy rates in India, also influenced the educational practices in Lakshadweep due to cultural and administrative proximity.
 
• Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep was followed closely by Chandigarh (86.43%) and Delhi (86.34%) in terms of literacy rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate:**

 
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of literate individuals in a specific age group, typically 7 years and above.
 
• It is calculated by dividing the number of literate individuals by the total population in the relevant age group and multiplying by 100.
 
 
 
• **Census of India:**
 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of India since 1872.
 
• It provides comprehensive data on demographics, socio-economic conditions, and literacy levels across the country.
 
 
 
• **Union Territories in India:**
 
 
• India has several Union Territories, which are administrative divisions governed directly by the central government.
 
• Examples include Lakshadweep, Delhi, Chandigarh, Puducherry, and others.
 
 
 
• **Education Policies:**
 
 
• Programs like Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) and the Right to Education Act have contributed significantly to improving literacy rates in India.
 
• Special focus on remote regions like Lakshadweep has helped bridge disparities in educational access.

questions.question: In which of the following types of regions, is the maximum temperature variation observed between a day and the same night?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Desert**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Deserts** experience the maximum temperature variation between day and night due to the lack of vegetation and moisture in the soil, resulting in rapid heating and cooling.
 
• During the day, deserts receive intense solar radiation, causing temperatures to soar to extreme levels.
 
• At night, the absence of clouds and moisture leads to rapid loss of heat through radiation, causing the temperature to drop significantly.
 
• The temperature difference between day and night in desert regions can be as high as 20°C to 30°C.
 
• Examples of deserts with high diurnal temperature variations include the Sahara Desert, Thar Desert, and the Mojave Desert.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diurnal Temperature Variation:**

 
 
• It refers to the difference between the highest and lowest temperatures within a single day.
 
• Regions with dry air and minimal vegetation, such as deserts, exhibit the highest diurnal temperature variations.
 
 
 
• **Role of Vegetation and Moisture:**
 
 
• Vegetation and moisture act as insulators, moderating the temperature variation by absorbing heat during the day and releasing it at night.
 
• Lack of these factors in deserts leads to extremes in temperature changes.
 
 
 
• **Heat Radiation Process:**
 
 
• During the night, heat from the surface radiates back into the atmosphere, leading to rapid cooling in regions like deserts.
 
• Cloud cover and humidity slow down this process in other regions, reducing temperature variation.
 
 
 
• **Comparison to Coastal Areas:**
 
 
• Coastal regions exhibit minimal temperature variation between day and night due to the moderating effect of nearby water bodies.
 
• Water has a high heat capacity, absorbing and releasing heat slowly, stabilizing the temperature.
